# jcs-admit

> Admit raw JSON bytes before RFC 8785 canonicalization, hashing or signing.

Start with crate version 0.1.1 and Rust 1.74 or newer. `cargo add jcs-admit@=0.1.1` selects that release.

Pass the original byte slice to `admit`, `admit_ijson` or `admit_with`. Admission preserves the evidence needed to reject repeated decoded keys, invalid strings and exceeded depth or size limits before canonicalization. A parsed map has already lost repeated-key evidence.

For a producer, sign or hash the returned canonical bytes. For a verifier requiring canonical input, call `is_canonical_with` under the verification profile before hashing the received bytes. RFC 8785 uses IEEE-754 number formatting; for example, the default profile rewrites 9007199254740993 to 9007199254740992. The I-JSON profile refuses that integer.

## Start here

- [Quick start](https://github.com/probityai/jcs-admit/blob/main/README.md): Admit a document and inspect a duplicate-key refusal.
- [Version 0.1.1 API](https://docs.rs/jcs-admit/0.1.1/jcs_admit/): Admission functions, explicit options and error variants.
- [Design and evidence](https://github.com/probityai/jcs-admit/blob/main/docs/DESIGN.md): Raw-input checks, canonicalization and their test evidence.

## Run a comparison

- [APS byte comparison](https://github.com/probityai/jcs-admit/blob/main/interop/aps-canonical-bytes/README.md): Retained 8-case and 10-case canonical-byte runs.
- [Python byte profile](https://github.com/probityai/jcs-admit/blob/main/interop/rfc8785-py/README.md): Source-pinned independent byte cases and raw-input refusals.
- [Mutation sweep](https://github.com/probityai/jcs-admit/blob/main/docs/MUTATION-SWEEP.md): The check that detects each removed refusal.
- [Open Evidence Lab](https://probityai.github.io/agent-evidence-atlas/lab.html): Retained runs, operators, artifacts and rerun routes.

- [Contribution guide](https://github.com/probityai/jcs-admit/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): Build, test, lint and submit a change.
